title: unread-mail-is-not-kept
intention: A BaseDevice whose class declares no reader of its inbound mail keeps none of it: BaseDevice.receive writes to the inbound DataRecorder only when RECORDER_ON_READ is declared, so a mailbox nobody opens stops growing, and the inbound recorders already filled by undeclared holders are drained once.
why: Measured 2026-10-01: test_isolation reds at 273MB against its 150MB bound, blocking every tester PROVED crossing; 127MB of instance-space is inbound mail no device reads. Lived symptom: no tester ticket can reach PROVED, and every proof sandbox copies 127MB of trash.
traces_to: Law 9 and Law 7: test_isolation reds because instance-space is inflated by mail nobody reads, and that red blocks every PROVED crossing in the tester component. The ruling 'if it's not consumed, it's trash' (2026-09-30): recorded is not consumed.
how: In cairn/tools/base/device.py BaseDevice.receive: when type(self).RECORDER_ON_READ is None, skip the DataRecorder write (the 'received' emit and the accepted reply stay — the sender still learns the mail arrived). A device that wants its mail kept declares RECORDER_ON_READ ('drain' or 'hold') and RECORDER_READ_FREQUENCY_SECONDS, exactly the declaration ticket a4c2be029f49 already defined; the comment above the two class attributes says that undeclared now means unkept, citing the ruling 'if it's not consumed, it's trash' (2026-09-30, CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-heartbeat-probes-and-bus.md). Apply, once, after the build is sealed: for every ~/.cairn/devices/*/*/tools/data_recorder/inbound whose reading.json reads on_read null, remove the directory (records.jsonl and reading.json) — the records were never read and by the ruling are trash; removing reading.json lets the a4c2be029f49 probe reconcile its recorder-declares-no-reader troubles away. Proved by a new cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_unread_mail_is_not_kept.py over a fixture BaseDevice whose _recorder is preset to a scratch DataRecorder.
falsifier: RED if: (1) a fixture BaseDevice with RECORDER_ON_READ None, its _recorder preset to a scratch DataRecorder, receives one envelope and the scratch recorder then holds any record; (2) the same fixture with RECORDER_ON_READ 'hold' and RECORDER_READ_FREQUENCY_SECONDS 60 receives one envelope and the scratch recorder does not hold exactly one record carrying that envelope's id; (3) either fixture's receive does not return accepted True. Horizon: the tester seal of the new proof.
watchme: none, because cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_isolation.py is the receiver: its disk_bytes bound reds at every reseal while instance-space carries unread mail, and the build gate reads it at every PROVED crossing in the tester component
children: none, because the change is one guard in BaseDevice.receive plus a one-time drain; the _FeedbackDevice writer is a sibling ticket in its own component, not a child
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) How is the fixture device built? Subclass BaseDevice with intention/state/settings returning small dicts, as cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_chat_pane.py does. (2) How does the proof avoid the live instance root? Set dev._recorder = DataRecorder(scratch_dir('unread_mail_fixture_') / 'inbound', expected_read_frequency_seconds=..., on_read=...) before receive; _get_recorder returns it. (3) What envelope? {'id': 'env-fixture-1', 'sender': 'proof', 'why': 'fixture mail', 'verb': '', 'body': {'k': 1}}. (4) Does emit need a bus? emit is called on every receive today; if it raises without a shim, the tooth reports that verbatim. (5) PROVES = {ticket: {'1':..., '2':..., '3':...}}.

chart_claim.filled_by: CC chart chain (orient ebbdda69cb8a .. validate c8ffcfb22cb4, each learned)

decisions.text: STEP 1, the red proof. Write cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_unread_mail_is_not_kept.py, runnable as a script: at the end, from cairn.tools.proof_coverage import print_teeth_main; print_teeth_main(__file__) under if __name__ == '__main__' (the same runner cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_fixme.py uses). PROVES = {'ae8d2bfb08e2': {'1': 'test_an_undeclared_device_keeps_no_mail', '2': 'test_a_declared_device_keeps_exactly_the_mail_it_got', '3': 'test_both_devices_accept_the_mail'}}. Fixture classes at module level: class _Undeclared(BaseDevice) with intention() returning {'what': 'unread mail fixture', 'why': 'prove undeclared mail is not kept'}, state() returning {'resting': 'test'}, settings() returning {} (the shape cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_chat_pane.py uses at line 22); class _Declared(_Undeclared) with RECORDER_ON_READ = 'hold' and RECORDER_READ_FREQUENCY_SECONDS = 60. from cairn.tools.base.device import BaseDevice at module top; resolve DataRecorder inside each tooth via importlib.import_module('cairn.tools.data_recorder.data_recorder').DataRecorder. A helper _fire(cls) does: dev = cls(); dev._recorder = DataRecorder(scratch_dir('unread_mail_fixture_') / 'inbound', expected_read_frequency_seconds=cls.RECORDER_READ_FREQUENCY_SECONDS, on_read=cls.RECORDER_ON_READ); reply = dev.receive({'id': 'env-fixture-1', 'sender': 'proof', 'why': 'fixture mail', 'verb': '', 'body': {'k': 1}}); return reply, dev._recorder.read(). scratch_dir is from cairn.devices.tester.scratch import scratch_dir (cairn/devices/tester/scratch.py:73, a plain function returning a fresh Path). Tooth 1: records == []. Tooth 2: len(records) == 1 and records[0]['envelope_id'] == 'env-fixture-1'. Tooth 3: both replies have accepted True. Run it: tooth 1 red before the build, teeth 2 and 3 green. Commit it red.

STEP 2, the build in cairn/tools/base/device.py BaseDevice.receive (line ~257): wrap the self._get_recorder().write({...}) call in if type(self).RECORDER_ON_READ is not None:, leaving self.emit('received', ...) and the return {'accepted': True, 'device': self.device_id} unconditional. Rewrite the comment block above RECORDER_READ_FREQUENCY_SECONDS (line ~230) to add: undeclared now means unkept — a device that declares no RECORDER_ON_READ keeps none of its inbound mail (ruling 'if it's not consumed, it's trash', 2026-09-30, CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-heartbeat-probes-and-bus.md; ticket ae8d2bfb08e2), so a device that wants its mail kept declares both attributes. Update receive's docstring to match. Run test_unread_mail_is_not_kept.py green twice, then every cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_*.py, all of which must stay green; commit (the pre-commit reseal can take over 10 minutes; run it in the background); seal with python3 -m cairn.devices.tester.cli --seal cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_unread_mail_is_not_kept.py; commit.

STEP 3, the one-time drain, after the seal is committed. For every directory d matching ~/.cairn/devices/*/*/tools/data_recorder/inbound: read d/reading.json; when it is absent or its on_read is null, shutil.rmtree(d). Print each removed path and its size (du -sb before), and the total. This is instance-space, not git; the records were never read (last_read null everywhere, measured 2026-10-01) and are trash by the ruling. Then measure: du -s --exclude=logs --exclude='*venv*' ~/.cairn, and run python3 cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_isolation.py and record its disk_bytes line in the PROVEME note (test_isolation is the tester's proof: measured, not edited, RULE 1).

D3's measurements are recorded in the WHY text of the BUILDME->PROVEME crossing, the one free-text argument of that crossing, which the transition journals verbatim into cairn/tools/base/history.json. The builder writes that text as: 'disk_bytes before=<du -sb ~/.cairn excluding logs and venvs, taken before the drain> after=<the same du after the drain>; drained=<count of inbound dirs removed>; test_isolation <green|red>'. No other file or field records it; there is no separate note command.

Settles D2's docstring, D3's line and D4's mechanism. (a) D2: receive's docstring gains exactly this sentence: 'The envelope is kept in the inbound DataRecorder only when this device's class declares RECORDER_ON_READ; a device that declares no reader keeps none of its mail (ticket ae8d2bfb08e2), and the reply is the same either way.' The guard tests RECORDER_ON_READ alone (D2's if); RECORDER_READ_FREQUENCY_SECONDS is still passed to the recorder as today. (b) D3's 'disk_bytes line' is the line test_isolation.py prints that begins '  scratch: ' and reads '<n>MB disk, <m> entries' (printed at cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_isolation.py:315, the per-proof sandbox size, asserted under 150MB at line 317); the builder copies the <n>MB figure from it, plus the final green/red line. (c) D4's crossing is made by the builder's crossing script, which calls cairn.tools.base.transitions.emit(ticket_state, 'PROVEME', history_path=cairn/tools/base/history.json, state_path=cairn/tools/base/state.json, ticket='ae8d2bfb08e2', actor='cc', proven_by=['cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_unread_mail_is_not_kept.py']) and writes the new state back through the artifact door with that crossing's why text; the why text is D4's line with 'sandbox=<n>MB' appended.

CORRECTS D4 and D5, measured 2026-10-01 at cairn/tools/base/transitions.py:1940: emit(workflow_str, target, *, history_path=None, state_path=None, node_class_root=..., **journal_extra) has no why parameter of its own; every extra keyword is journal_extra and is written into the crossing's record in history.json (the records there already carry ticket, actor, proven_by that way). So the PROVEME crossing passes the measurement line as why=<line>: emit(t['workflow_and_state'], 'PROVEME', history_path='cairn/tools/base/history.json', state_path='cairn/tools/base/state.json', ticket='ae8d2bfb08e2', actor='cc', proven_by=['cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_unread_mail_is_not_kept.py'], why=<line>), where t is the ticket JSON read from CairnCommons/tickets/ae8d2bfb08e2-*.json and the returned string is written back to that file through cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write(path, text, verb='cast', why=<the same line>). D3's order is: (1) du -sb --exclude=logs --exclude='*venv*' ~/.cairn = before; (2) the drain; (3) the same du = after; (4) test_isolation.py.

D1's import placement, measured 2026-10-01 in the proof as written (cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_unread_mail_is_not_kept.py): the helper is def _fire(cls): at line 51 and its FIRST line, line 52, is DataRecorder = importlib.import_module('cairn.tools.data_recorder.data_recorder').DataRecorder — the import is inside _fire's body, so every tooth that calls _fire (lines 62, 67, 74) has it in scope, and a module that fails to import reds the tooth that fires, not the file.
